text:
sylvie: Heads-up — seeing a flurry of tiny pods stuck Pending in us-west2, all GPU requests 0.125/0.25 but scheduler keeps placing them on nodes with incompatible slot granularity and they get evicted quickly. Looks like a mismatch between our slot-size allocator and the new gpu-slab v2 packing logic.
raj: Ugh, saw that too. Patch from yesterday changed node labeling for slab-size, maybe scheduler nonlocal scoring doesn't respect it. @mina you on call? :eyes:
mina: yep I'm looking. Quick dump of one stuck pod and the node it tried: 
mina: ```
kubectl describe pod tiny-runner-7f9c -n training
Events:
  Type     Reason         Age   From               Message
  ----     ------         ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling 2m    default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 4 node(s) had insecure GPU topology, 6 node(s) had insufficient allocatable GPUs (requested: 0.25, available: 0.125).
```
mina: node label on target node: `gpu.redwood/shelf-granularity=0.5` but the pod requested 0.25 so scheduler thinks it's incompatible due to our custom predicate.
sylvie: Wait — predicate uses `<=` incorrectly? That would treat 0.25 as >0.5 in string compare if label parsed as string. Could be parsing bug when we switched to slab v2.
raj: I pulled logs from scheduler around the decision time: 
raj: ```
I0323 12:07:11 scheduler.go:324] scoring pod tiny-runner-7f9c on node gpu-node-42: predicate GPUGranularity failed: requested=0.25 node_label=0.5 (parsed as "50")
```
raj: parser turned percentages into integers in the new codepath. :facepalm:
joel: That explains the mass evictions. If scheduler rejects nodes incorrectly, pods get scheduled elsewhere then evicted when attach fails, or sit Pending. Cost spike too — we've been double-scheduling some batches.
mina: I'm going to revert the string->int change in the predicate and add unit tests. Rolling a canary in apse2 first.
sylvie: Can we also add a telemetry gauge for 'granularity_matches' so ops can alert before evictions blow up? We missed this earlier.
raj: +1. Also set a short-term workaround: set `gpu.redwood/shelf-granularity` on warmpool nodes to match smaller slot sizes (0.25) so they accept tiny pods until fix lands. Ops script: `kubectl label nodes -l warmpool=true gpu.redwood/shelf-granularity=0.25`
mina: deploying fix branch now, will post CI link.
infra-bot: deploy job started: build-ops/slot-parse-fix #847 -> staging (apse2)
sylvie: Nice. If canary looks good, promote to us-west2 main. Also we should run a re-scheduler job to re-evaluate Pending pods once fix is live. Suggest `kubectl get pods -n training --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl delete` to trigger rescheduling.
joel: Be careful deleting — would prefer a controlled requeueer to avoid thundering herd. I'll hack a small controller that pokes the scheduler to re-evaluate 100 pods/second.
raj: For immediate relief, I've adjusted eviction threshold to 30s in the eviction controller for those namespaces so we don't repeatedly churn while fix propagates.
mina: Canary passed in apse2, no rejects for new tiny pods. Patching main clusters in 10m.
sylvie: Thanks. Postmortem action items: 1) unit tests for granularity parse edgecases, 2) telemetry/alert on predicate-mismatch rate, 3) emergency warmpool label playbook, 4) improve requeue mechanism to avoid delete-via-kubectl.
joel: I'll own #4, put a quick RFC in eng-platform channel tomorrow.
mina: Rolling to us-west2 now. ETA 8m.
sylvie: Great work. Please ping if any residual evictions. :thumbsup:
